full_judgment: 18. We are entirely in agreement with observation of his Lordship A.T.M. Masued (J). In the case of State vs. Nawab Ali Biswas, reported in (1961) 13 DLR 646 several persons were tried and convicted under section 302/34 B.P.C. and condemned prisoner Nawab Ali Biswas was sentenced to death but so far other appellants were concerned they were sentenced to transportation for life. On the ground that condemned prisoner Nawab Ali Biswas played active role in the commission or the murder. But death sentence imposed on Nawab Ali Biswas was commuted to life imprisonment not on consideration of the fact that execution of death sentence was delayed but on consideration that Nawab Ali suffered mental torture and agony for having remained under the order of death sentence though legally and morally, he ought to have been treated on equal footing with other appellants. So to bring punishment imposed on Nawab Ali at par with other appellants sentence of death awarded to Nawab Ali was substituted by life imprisonment. Their Lordships did not hold the view that delay in execution of death sentence for want of confirmation will itself constitute mitigating circumstance.
